title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page, 'situation abstraite des doubles réseaux'): M = Rep(G) is a ⊗-category over a field k, with a tower of fields k ⊂ K ⊂ L. T is a fibre functor over k and T' a fibre functor over K, with a ⊗-isomorphism φ: T⊗L ≅ T'⊗L. Put G = Aut⊗(T) and P = Isom⊗(T_K, T'), a right G_K-torsor, so that φ ∈ P(L). Archetype: k = Q, T = Betti, K = a number field or Q, T' = de Rham, L = C, φ = the period comparison.

For each object V, the L-space V⊗L carries two structures: the k-lattice V and the K-structure T'(V). The page studies V ∩ T'(V), the elements rational for both structures (modern: de Rham–Betti classes).

Trivial-torsor case. Choose ξ ∈ P(K) and write ξ = φg with g ∈ G(L), well defined modulo G(K). Let R ⊂ G_K be the Zariski closure of the image of T_K×T_K → G_K, (s,t) ↦ ts⁻¹.
- Previous page: x ∈ V ∩ T'(V) implies R ⊂ (G_x)_K, where G_x is the stabiliser of x.
- This page proves the converse by fpqc descent. T_K is faithfully flat over K, and the points s ∈ T_K(Λ) give s⁻¹x independent of s. So s⁻¹x descends to a well-determined point of V_K, which puts x in T'(V).
- Let S be the closure of p(R) under the projection p: G_K → G, and H the closed subgroup of G generated by S. Since (G_x)_K = p⁻¹(G_x), one gets x ∈ V∩T'(V) ⇔ R ⊂ (G_x)_K ⇔ S ⊂ G_x ⇔ H ⊂ G_x ⇔ x ∈ V^H.
- Hence V∩T'(V) = V^H.

Consequence. The functor Rep(G) = M → {L-vector spaces with a k-structure and a K-structure} ('structures vectorielles mixtes relatives à L/K/k') is fully faithful iff V∩T'(V) = V^G for all V. Apply this to Hom(V,W) = V*⊗W, using rigidity. So the functor is fully faithful iff V^H = V^G for every representation V.

General case (P arbitrary). Use the canonical bitorsor map P×_K P → G_K, (v,u) ↦ v⁻¹u. Composing it with φ×φ: Spec(L⊗_K L) → P×_K P gives a map to G_K whose closed image R_K is intrinsic, with no choice of ξ needed. The same descent argument gives V∩T'(V) = {x : R_K ⊂ (G_x)_K} = V^H, with the same conclusion as before.

Purpose. This is a Tannakian analysis of when the comparison ('period') data determine morphisms of motives. In effect it is the full-faithfulness of the de Rham–Betti realization, and a precursor to the Grothendieck period conjecture.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck stops, correctly, at 'V^H = V^G for all V' and does not claim H = G. These are genuinely different: for reductive G, a proper subgroup such as a Borel subgroup of SL2 satisfies V^B = V^G for all V. That is, H need only be an epimorphic subgroup of G (in the sense of Bien–Borel).
Minor gap: one must note that R contains the identity (take s = t), so S generates H, and that p is the base-change projection G_K → G. Both are harmless.
Full faithfulness also uses that the double structure on V*⊗W is induced compatibly; this is implicit in 'structures vectorielles mixtes'.

ideas.what: Category of 'double lattices': L-vector spaces with a k-structure and a K-structure, receiving a functor from a Tannakian category via a comparison isomorphism φ
ideas.modern_name: de Rham–Betti structures / category of (k,K,L)-comparison structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004, ch. 7); Bost–Charles (de Rham–Betti structures)
ideas.where_published: Period conjecture only mentioned in passing (footnote in Lang's Introduction to transcendental numbers, 1966); no published development

ideas.what: V∩T'(V) = V^H where H is the closed subgroup generated by the projection of the closed image of Spec(L⊗_K L) → P×_K P → G_K
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of the period point / Zariski closure of the period torsor; group of de Rham–Betti structure (G_dRB)
ideas.usually_credited_to: André; Bost–Charles; analogous to Katz/Deligne torsor description of Picard–Vessiot Galois groups

ideas.what: Criterion: the comparison functor is fully faithful iff V^H = V^G for all representations V
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of the realization functor ⇔ H is epimorphic in G (weak form of the Grothendieck period conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed in André 2004 and Bost–Charles (around 2016) in other forms

ideas.what: Descent argument identifying double-rational points with points whose stabiliser contains R

missed.claim: Full faithfulness of the de Rham–Betti (or general L/K/k comparison) realization is characterised exactly by V^H = V^G for all V, i.e. by H being an epimorphic subgroup of G, rather than by H = G. This is weaker than the period-torsor/generic-point formulation of the period conjecture. The later literature frames full faithfulness via equality of Tannakian groups and, to my knowledge, does not single out the notion of an epimorphic subgroup.
missed.quote: il faut et s. que pour tt V, V^H=V^G.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It separates the full-faithfulness conjecture for de Rham–Betti realizations (Bost–Charles, André) from the stronger torsor-density statement. It also suggests checking the gap between them through epimorphic-subgroup theory, which is relevant in the reductive case.

missed.claim: Intrinsic construction, for a non-trivial torsor P, of R_K as the closed image of Spec(L⊗_K L) → P×_K P → G_K via the bitorsor difference map, with V∩T'(V) = V^H. This is an early (1965) Tannakian formalism for the 'Galois group of the periods' in a relative tower k⊂K⊂L.
missed.quote: Spec(L)×_{Spec K}Spec(L)→P×_{Spec K}P→G_K ; l'image fermée R_K est donc définie intrinsèquement.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise antecedent of André's and Bost–Charles' formalism, and of the torsor description of differential Galois groups. It is relevant to crediting the Tannakian period formalism to Grothendieck in 1965.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, finished Tannakian computation in 1965 of de Rham–Betti double-rational classes as H-invariants, with a sharp full-faithfulness criterion that correctly does not overclaim H = G. The ideas are known in later form (André, Bost–Charles), but this explicit version and its date are not in the published record.
